summary: 100-foot steel fire tower near Stevenson, Jackson County, reported completed in July 1942; no later record or current status found.

events.note: Reported completed in a July 1, 1942 Alabama Journal item quoted by Forest Lookouts; the item credits the Alabama Conservation Department's division of forestry

evidence.supports: page names the Alabama Forestry Commission as agency
completed tower at Russell's Point near Stevenson, built by the Alabama Conservation Department's division of forestry
evidence.quote: A new forest fire lookout tower, at Russell's Point near Stevenson in Jackson County, has been completed by the Alabama Conservation Department's division of forestry.
The new observation post is a 100-foot steel tower.

evidence.supports: Forester Brooks Toler reported four more under construction
evidence.quote: Forester Brooks Toler reported that four additional ones are under construction

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The page header names the Alabama Forestry Commission; the quoted 1942 item credits the Alabama Conservation Department's division of forestry. The story gives the sources' wording and does not decide which name is right.

sources.title: Russell's Point
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com), quoting the Alabama Journal

notes_for_editor: Single secondary source: a Forest Lookouts page quoting a July 1, 1942 Alabama Journal item. The original newspaper was not read. Two WebSearch calls found no other record of this tower, and the NHLR crawl cache has no Russell's Point entry (a guessed NHLR URL returned 404). Brief record checks: source page and 30.5 m height (100 ft) match; agency matches the page header, but the 1942 item names a different body (see resolved_conflicts). The brief's coordinates (34.85397, -85.89942) were not checked against a source. Status and access are unknown and omitted; the story says no current source describes the site. Story is short because the record is short. Verification pass: the story now uses the past tense for the 1942 tower so it does not imply the tower stands today; the Toler name was confirmed on the page and is now in the evidence quote.
